lessons.title: Lesson 1: Setup Sprint, Open Every Door
lessons.goal: Reagan creates the starting workspace first: Claude access, Codex access, Telegram installed, and a proof folder ready before the concepts get heavy.
sections: Why this comes first
This course starts with a real setup win. Before learning all the terms, open the tools, create the proof folder, and make sure you can come back tomorrow without starting over.
Create the AI Workspace folder

On the MacBook, open Finder and create a folder named AI Workspace in Documents. Inside it, make Proof, Notes, and Exports folders. Keep screenshots, Markdown files, and progress exports there before backing them up to Google Drive.
MacBook ready check

Before the course starts, charge the MacBook, connect WiFi, update Chrome, install Telegram Desktop if it is missing, bookmark Claude, OpenAI or Codex, Google Drive, and this course page, then clean the Downloads folder so setup files are easy to find.
Open the tools

Use cloud tools first because we do not know this MacBook's RAM. Open Claude in the browser. Open Codex or OpenAI with the account CJ provides. Open Telegram Desktop or Telegram Web. Do not install local models, Docker, Ollama, LM Studio, or anything heavy unless CJ approves it live.
Cloud model rule

The default path is browser based. If a video shows a terminal or CLI install, treat that as a demo unless CJ specifically says to run it on Reagan's MacBook. The win is access, safe prompts, saved proof, and a clean resume path, not turning her laptop into a server.
Start the proof log
Create proof-log.md. Add today’s date, the tool names, and one line for each status: Claude open, Codex open, Telegram installed, Drive folder created.
Submit

Submit one screenshot of the AI Workspace folder, one screenshot showing each cloud tool is reachable, and one note confirming the MacBook ready check is done. Hide private values. If a login needs CJ, write waiting on CJ next to that item.

sections: Warm up
Claude is the thinking partner. Use it for writing, planning, summarizing, and explaining. It is not a password vault and it does not replace judgment.
Mac browser setup
Use Chrome or Safari on the MacBook. Sign in, bookmark Claude, and keep the AI Workspace folder open in Finder so saved notes and screenshots go to the same place every time.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 5:19 Anthropic video. Pause after the first prompt example and write what made the prompt clear.
Build
Ask Claude to create a 5 step plan for setting up your AI workspace on a MacBook using cloud tools only. Then ask it to make the plan shorter and more direct.
Save
Paste the final plan into prompts.md and write one sentence about what made the second version better.
Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Claude open in the Mac browser and paste the final 5 step cloud setup plan into your workbook.

sections: Warm up
Codex is for building, editing, reviewing, and checking work. Think of it as another smart teammate, not a magic button.
Setup

Start with the cloud or account based Codex path CJ provides. Confirm you can open Codex and start a safe sample task. If the official video shows CLI commands, watch them for context first. Do not run terminal installs on the MacBook unless CJ approves them.
Mac safety rule

Unknown RAM means no local model work today. Codex is here to review, edit, and build from cloud access. If terminal access is needed, CJ can demo it while Reagan records what changed in proof-log.md.
Watch with purpose
Watch the OpenAI video. Write one thing Codex does that feels different from a normal chat.
Build
Give Codex a simple sample task: review this checklist for clarity. Use fake content, not private CJ business data.
Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Codex or OpenAI access and 3 bullets on when you would choose Codex instead of Claude. Add one line confirming no heavy local install was started.

sections: Warm up

Telegram is the front door. The agent is the worker behind it. BotFather can create a bot account, but CJ's Hermes setup connects the real agent. Today the goal is cloud connected access, not running Hermes locally on the MacBook.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 1:34 BotFather clip. Write down what BotFather creates and what it does not create.
Setup

Install Telegram Desktop from the official Telegram site or use Telegram Web if needed. Create the Telegram bot only if CJ asks. Save the bot name. Never paste a bot token into public docs, screenshots, or the workbook.
Hermes connection

Follow CJ's guided internal setup for the Telegram agent front door. If a token, gateway setting, or admin step is needed, CJ handles it. Reagan records the bot name, what worked, and how to reopen the chat tomorrow.
Proof
Submit a screenshot of the Telegram agent chat working, with any private token hidden. Add the bot name, date, MacBook setup status, and resume steps to proof-log.md.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: LLMs, Agents, Skills, Commands, Tools, and MCPs

video.title: What are AI agents? AI Agents Explained in 2 minutes
video.purpose: Quick visual intro to agents before CJ examples.

lessons.goal: Reagan can explain the core agent language in plain English and connect each word to the setup she just built.
sections: Start from what you built

Look at your setup proof. Claude is a cloud LLM. Codex is a build focused AI tool. Telegram is a front door. Hermes is the agent system behind that front door. The MacBook is just the workstation, not the brain.
LLM vs agent
An LLM thinks and answers. An agent thinks and acts with tools, memory, rules, and a goal. Simple line: chatbot answers, agent gets work done.
Cloud vs local
A cloud model runs on someone else's servers through the browser or app. A local model runs on the laptop and needs more RAM and setup. For this course, use cloud models unless CJ says otherwise.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 2 minute agent clip. Write down the first moment where the video moves from talking to doing.
Building blocks
A command tells the agent what to do. A skill is a saved best practice. A tool lets the agent touch the outside world. An MCP is a clean way to connect tools and data.
Build
Add a glossary to my-ai-workspace.md with: LLM, agent, command, skill, tool, MCP, wiki, vault, closeout, Drive backup. Use your own words.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Markdown, Saved Work, Drive Backup, and Closeout

video.title: Markdown in 2 Minutes
video.purpose: Show Markdown as simple structured text before she builds workspace files.

lessons.goal: Reagan builds the habit of saving useful work in Markdown, backing it up, and closing the loop with proof.
sections: Markdown is the playbook
Markdown is plain text with structure. Use headings, bullets, links, screenshots, and checklists. It keeps work readable for people and useful for agents.
Karpathy style setup
Start every workspace with clear context, examples, constraints, and proof. The agent should not guess where things live or what good looks like.
Drive backup
Local files are not enough. On the MacBook, keep the working folder in Documents, then back up the AI Workspace folder to Google Drive so Rea can recover progress and CJ can review proof.
Mac folder habit
Use Finder the same way every time: Documents > AI Workspace for work, Downloads for temporary files, and Google Drive for backup. If a file lands in Downloads, move it before closing the laptop.
Closeout habit
Every session ends with what changed, where it lives, proof, and the next step. If it is not written down, it did not happen.
Build
Create or update my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, and closeout.md. Add today’s Mac setup notes, cloud tool links, and one clean next step.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: First Project, My AI Workspace

video.title: How To Use Google Drive
video.purpose: Show the backup habit for files, screenshots, and proof.

lessons.goal: Reagan finishes with a real AI workspace, saved progress, a Drive backup, and a clear resume point.
sections: Project brief

Build My AI Workspace for a MacBook cloud setup. It should prove she can log into Claude, use Codex or OpenAI, message the Telegram agent, explain the agent language, save Markdown files, and back everything up to Drive.
Before Reagan leaves tomorrow
She should be able to close the MacBook, reopen it, open Documents > AI Workspace, open the course bookmark, open the Drive backup, and message the Telegram agent without CJ hunting for files.
Progress save
Use the Save progress button in this course. Download the progress file. Upload it to the AI Workspace folder in Google Drive.
Drive backup
Back up my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, closeout.md, the glossary, and screenshots to Drive. The rule is simple: local work plus cloud proof.
Closeout
Write one closeout note: what was set up, what worked, what is still missing, where the files live, and what the next step is.
Submit
Submit the Drive folder link or screenshot, the downloaded progress file, the final closeout note, and one MacBook resume checklist showing exactly how to start again tomorrow.

qualityRules: Lesson 1 must start with setup and proof before heavy concepts.
Every lesson must have at least one relevant visual aid: video, graphic, docs card, internal walkthrough, or useful combination.
Quiz correct answers must be varied. Do not make every correct answer A.
Prefer short YouTube clips over generic link cards when a credible short clip exists.
Do not teach tools or frameworks we do not use in CJ operations.
Every setup lesson must include a save, backup, and resume habit.
